overview:
Broadcom's WatchTower platform provides a comprehensive picture of mainframe health and performance. With its integrated real-time information streaming (z/IRIS), teams can anticipate failures based on past patterns, prevent small issues from becoming outages, and proactively manage z/OS operations.

This WatchTower z/IRIS integration collects metrics, logs, and traces via OpenTelemetry, and includes out-of-the-box content for seamless observability in Datadog:
- Monitor z/OS systems and applications using WatchTower's curated and customizable dashboards.
- Enable alerts on resource contention and application anomalies with WatchTower's recommended mainframe monitors.
- Enrich mainframe logs using the included log pipeline for easier analysis and correlation.
setup:
### Prerequisite

Verify that WatchTower z/IRIS is installed and running. Refer to the WatchTower z/IRIS Installation documentation on the [TechDocs Portal][1] for more information about installing z/IRIS in your environment.

### Installation

1. **Configure the OpenTelemetry Collector**

   - Configure the OTLP receiver
   
   WatchTower z/IRIS can export telemetry over HTTP or gRPC. Refer to the  z/IRIS IronTap configuration to verify the appropriate receiver is configured.
   
   - [Enable OTLP logs ingestion][2]
   - Add a Transform Processor to set the source of OTLP logs from z/IRIS

   ```yaml
     transform/datadog: 
      log_statements:
        - context: log
          statements:
            # set resource attribute if the instrumentation_scope name matches
            - set(resource.attributes["datadog.log.source"], "ziris") where scope.name == "com.broadcom.ziris.irontap"
   ```

   Add a transformation to prefix all metrics streamed from z/IRIS with `ziris.`:

   ```yaml
       metric_statements:
        - context: metric
          statements:
            # Concat "ziris" and the current metric name with a "." separator
            - set(name, Concat(["ziris", name], ".")) where scope.name == "com.broadcom.ziris.irontap"
   ```

2. [Configure the Datadog Exporter and Connector][3]

   Follow Datadog's documentation to add the Datadog exporter to your collector configuration and provide your API key.
   Add the processors `transform/datadog`  to the z/IRIS pipelines exporting signals to your Datadog tenant.

3. Launch the collector and verify in Datadog that the renamed metrics (`ziris.*`) are appearing in the [Metrics Explorer][4] and verify that mainframe traces and spans are streaming.

4. In Datadog, open the WatchTower z/IRIS integration tile and click **Install**.

   Dashboards will be cloned into your organization, and the monitors will be available on the [Monitor Templates][5] page.
   
5.  In Datadog, open Log explorer and verify that the z/IRIS custom group facets is available for filtering.

[1]: https://techdocs.broadcom.com/
[2]: https://docs.datadoghq.com/opentelemetry/setup/otlp_ingest_in_the_agent/?tab=host#enabling-otlp-logs-ingestion
[3]: https://docs.datadoghq.com/opentelemetry/setup/collector_exporter/install/#2---configure-the-datadog-exporter-and-connector
[4]: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer
[5]: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/templates

metrics.name: ziris.http.server.request.duration
metrics.description: The aggregated  distribution of duration for HTTP server requests in z/OS Connect APIs

metrics.name: ziris.irontap.correlation.active_correlations
metrics.description: Number of child/downstream correlation objects kept in memory until a matching parent/upstream part is found. The maximum number of active correlations is derived from the irontap.correlation.active-correlations configuration.

metrics.name: ziris.irontap.correlation.CICS_PERFORMANCE_TO_CICS_EXCEPTION.available
metrics.description: Number of available correlations before the capacity is reached for correlating CICS perfromance records to CICS Exception records.

metrics.name: ziris.irontap.correlation.CICS_TO_DB2.available
metrics.description: Number of available correlations before the capacity is reached for correlating CICS performance records to Db2 records.

metrics.name: ziris.irontap.correlation.CICS_TO_MQ.available
metrics.description: Number of available correlations before the capacity is reached for correlating CICS performance records to MQ  records.

metrics.name: ziris.irontap.correlation.SDSF.available
metrics.description: Number of available correlations before the capacity is reached for correlating SMF Type 30 records

metrics.name: ziris.irontap.correlation.SDSF.completed
metrics.description: Number of completed correlations for SMF 30 records. "Completed" means that the correlation was completed either successfully or unsuccessfully. If the correlation processing fails, it is by definition not completed, and the counter will not increment.

metrics.name: ziris.irontap.correlation.SDSF.started
metrics.description: Number of started correlations for SMF 30 correlations  "Started" means that a child/downstream part of one (or more) use cases has been found, so z/IRIS IronTap tries to find a matching parent/upstream part. If a matching downstream part is found, both sides are correlated.

metrics.name: ziris.irontap.correlation.SDSF.succeeded
metrics.description: Number of successful correlations for SMF 30. "Successful" means that for a correlation, the upstream part and the downstream part were successfully identified and correlated.

metrics.name: ziris.irontap.correlation.seen_correlators
metrics.description: Number of (parent/upstream) correlators kept in memory to be matched with possible incoming (child/downstream) correlators. The maximum number of seen correlators is derived from the irontap.correlation.correlation-info-capacity configuration.

metrics.name: ziris.irontap.correlation.SMF201_TO_CICS.available
metrics.description: Number of available correlations before the capacity is reached for correlating z/IRIS Type 210 records to CICS Performance records.

metrics.name: ziris.irontap.correlation.started_correlations
metrics.description: Same as "irontap.correlation.[use-case].started" but for all use cases combined.

metrics.name: ziris.irontap.correlation.ZCON_TO_CICS.available
metrics.description: Number of available correlations before the capacity is reached for correlating z/OS Connect records to CICS Performance records.

metrics.name: ziris.irontap.correlation.ZCON_TO_CICS.completed
metrics.description: Number of completed correlations for z/OS Connect to CICS records. "Completed" means that the correlation was completed either successfully or unsuccessfully. If the correlation processing fails, it is by definition not completed, and the counter will not increment.

metrics.name: ziris.irontap.correlation.ZCON_TO_CICS.started
metrics.description: Number of started correlations for z/OS COnnect to CICS correlations. "Started" means that a child/downstream part of one (or more) use cases has been found, so z/IRIS IronTap tries to find a matching parent/upstream part. If a matching downstream part is found, both sides are correlated.

metrics.name: ziris.irontap.correlation.ZCON_TO_CICS.succeeded
metrics.description: Number of successful correlations for z/OS Connect to CICS records. "Successful" means that for a correlation, the upstream part and the downstream part were successfully identified and correlated.

metrics.name: ziris.irontap.correlation.ZCON_TO_DB2.available
metrics.description: Number of available correlations before the capacity is reached for correlating z/OS Connect records to Db2 records.
